title: Debugging a check-then-act idempotency race condition
notes: Typical debugging session: symptom -> root cause -> fix -> verification -> pending follow-up.

turns.text: Ingest requests are occasionally creating two transcript rows for the same session_id when the client retries fast. Can you look into it?

Looking at the ingest route... I see the idempotency check does a SELECT then an INSERT in two separate steps — if two requests race, both can pass the SELECT before either INSERT commits. That's a classic check-then-act race condition.
I'll switch to an atomic 'INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING' inside a transaction, then read back whichever row won. That way concurrent requests can no longer both slip through.
Let's test it — fire 20 concurrent requests with the same idempotency key.

Ran a script with 20 concurrent POSTs, same Idempotency-Key, against the ingest endpoint. Before the fix: 3 duplicate rows. After the fix: exactly 1 row, the other 19 correctly got a 200 idempotent replay.
Great, ship it. Also we should add a regression test for this — can you do that next?
Noted — I'll add a concurrency regression test (fire N parallel requests with the same idempotency key, assert exactly one row created) in the next session; ran out of time this session.

gold_atoms.text: The ingest idempotency check had a check-then-act race condition: SELECT then INSERT as separate steps let two concurrent requests both pass the SELECT before either INSERT committed, producing duplicate transcript rows.
Fix duplicate transcript rows by using an atomic INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING inside a transaction, then reading back the winning row.
Verified the fix by firing 20 concurrent POSTs with the same Idempotency-Key against the ingest endpoint.
Before the fix, 20 concurrent requests with the same Idempotency-Key produced 3 duplicate rows; after the fix, exactly 1 row was created and the other 19 got a 200 idempotent replay.
Add a regression test that fires N concurrent requests with the same idempotency key and asserts exactly one row is created.
